subject: fix(web): scrub a session's on-disk artifacts in the delete endpoint
prompt: Deleting a session from the web dashboard (the per-session DELETE call the UI makes) removes it from the database, but its files stay on disk in the profile's transcript folder: the `<id>.jsonl` transcript, the gateway's `request_dump_<id>_*.json` dumps, and the older-format `session_<id>.json` snapshot, which can contain plaintext secrets. It happens for the default profile and for a named profile selected with `?profile=<name>`. Deleting from the CLI does remove the transcript and the dumps, but even there (and when pruning old conversations) a legacy `session_<id>.json` snapshot is left behind. Deleting a session should remove all of its on-disk files, in the profile it belongs to, without touching another session's files (for example one whose id merely starts with the same text).

subject: fix(curator): purge ages archives by the newer of archived_at and dir mtime
prompt: I archived one of my skills, later moved its folder out of `skills/.archive/` back into `skills/` by hand to use it again, and then archived it again with the manual archive subcommand. Minutes later, the `purge` subcommand that permanently deletes archived skills older than N days (`purge --days 30 --yes`) deleted it, even though it had only just been archived and its folder in `.archive/` was brand new. A skill should not be purged until it has really been archived for longer than the TTL. Archives made by older Hermes versions, whose folders still carry the skill's last-edit time, must still not be purged early either.

subject: fix(agent): classify NVIDIA NIM serde rejection of list-type tool content
prompt: I use Hermes with the NVIDIA provider (NVIDIA NIM, model moonshotai/kimi-k3) and a tool that returns a screenshot (computer use). The next model request fails with: `HTTP 400: Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: data did not match any variant of untagged enum ChatCompletionRequestToolMessageContent at line 1 column 1974809`. Hermes treats this as a permanent request error, so every retry sends the same image-bearing tool result and fails the same way for the rest of the session. When Xiaomi MiMo, Alibaba or OpenCode Go reject image content inside tool results, Hermes recognises it, turns the tool result into text, remembers that provider/model, and retries; NVIDIA's wording should get the same recovery. Other NIM deserialization errors that are not about tool message content should still be treated as ordinary request errors.

subject: fix(tui_gateway): stop the previous notification poller on agent rebuild
prompt: In the terminal UI (TUI), every time the agent of a live session is rebuilt (switching model mid-session with /model, resuming, or a late MCP refresh), one more background notification poller thread for that session is left running; a thread dump shows several `tui-notif-poller-<session id>` threads. The extra pollers keep consuming background-completion notifications and driving /loop, /heartbeat and bot delivery for that session, and closing the session only stops the newest one. After a rebuild there should be exactly one live notification poller per session, and the previous one should exit.

subject: fix(memory): one teardown claim shared by session-end shutdown and soft release
prompt: With an external memory provider configured, I send /new in a messaging chat (e.g. Telegram) through the gateway. The provider's end-of-session extraction for the old conversation is slow, so /new stops waiting for its cleanup after its timeout (30 s), and the cached agent for that chat is then evicted. The eviction shuts the memory provider down while the extraction is still running against it, and when the extraction finally finishes the provider is shut down a second time. Expected: while an end-of-session cleanup is still in progress, eviction should leave the shutdown to it, so the extraction completes against a live provider and the provider is shut down exactly once, afterwards.
